title: Egg and Meat Sandwich on Wheat Bread

content.title: About
content.content: An egg and meat sandwich on wheat bread is a nutritious snack consisting of whole‑grain bread, a boiled egg, tender cooked meat (such as chicken breast or ham), and optionally a slice of lettuce and a light sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat bread provides slow‑release energy thanks to its complex carbohydrates.
Eggs are one of the most affordable sources of complete protein, containing all essential amino acids.
Meat adds iron and vitamin B12, important for blood formation and nervous system function.
The protein‑carbohydrate combo makes this sandwich a popular post‑workout option.
Traditionally such sandwiches are served in school cafeterias and at sports events.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and meat together provide a substantial amount of complete protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and egg supply vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat, especially beef, is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of complex carbs from wheat bread and protein helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain bread adds fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed meats or sauces can raise the salt level, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat or eggs may harbor salmonella; ensure they are fully cooked.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, which is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. It can be served warm or cold, with added lettuce, tomato, or mustard according to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, separate the ingredients: store bread separately and keep meat and egg chilled.
